name: Internet Explorer file:///
location: IE6-7: %USERPROFILE%\Local Settings\History\History.IE5; IE8-9: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\History\History.IE5; IE10-11 and Windows 10+: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\WebCache\WebCacheV*.dat
purpose: Internet Explorer's history databases record local and remote (network share) file-path access per user, logged as file:/// URL entries. Because the underlying database formats persist across OS versions, some of this evidence can still be recovered even on Windows 11+ systems that no longer ship Internet Explorer.
key_fields: Per-user History.IE5 / WebCacheV*.dat container, isolating evidence by profile
Access timestamp associated with each history entry
Container/partition table inside WebCacheV*.dat (IE10+) separating history, cache, and cookies within the single ESE file
normal_baseline: file:/// entries pointing to local documents, downloads, or mapped/UNC network shares the user has legitimately opened through Explorer or an application's 'Recent Files' list, consistent with the account's normal file-access pattern.
anomalies: file:/// entries for sensitive network shares (finance, HR, executive) outside the user's documented job function
A burst of file:/// entries covering many distinct file paths in a short window, consistent with bulk browsing or staging ahead of exfiltration
file:/// entries referencing servers or shares the user has no legitimate business reason to access

Entries present despite Internet Explorer being uninstalled or never used on the account, indicating the access occurred through another shell component (e.g., Explorer, Office) that also writes to this database
anti_forensic_notes: History.IE5/WebCacheV*.dat can be cleared through Internet Explorer's 'Clear browsing data' or a general privacy cleaner, and WebCacheV*.dat also self-purges older records as a fixed-size ESE database fills. Because file:/// entries are generated regardless of whether Internet Explorer is installed or used, a missing or unusually sparse database on a system with clear evidence of local or network file activity can itself point to targeted clearing of this artifact rather than genuine non-use.
interpretation: Entries are recorded as file:///C:/<directory>/<filename>.<ext>. A file:/// entry does not mean the file was opened in a web browser-Explorer, Office's 'Recent Files', and other shell components generate the same records when a local or network file is accessed, so this artifact is general file-access evidence rather than proof of browser activity.
